frames.caption: An envelope fits inside another if both width and height are strictly smaller. How many can be nested?

Sort by width ascending, and for equal widths by height descending. Now any increasing sequence of heights automatically has increasing widths, and two envelopes of the same width can never both be picked (their heights go down).
Read height 3. tails is empty, so 3 starts the first subsequence (length 1).
Read height 4. 4 is bigger than every tail, so it extends the longest subsequence (length 2).
Read height 7. 7 is bigger than every tail, so it extends the longest subsequence (length 3).
Read height 4. 4 equals tails[1], so nothing changes (the subsequence must be strictly increasing).
3 envelopes nest: 2x3 → 5x4 → 6x7. Without the descending tie-break, 6x4 and 6x7 would wrongly count as nested.
